question: Atmospheric pressure and the rate of transpiration are _________
solution:
The correct answer is __**inversely proportional.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric pressure** and the **rate of transpiration** are **inversely proportional.**
 
• This means that as the atmospheric pressure** increases,** the rate of transpiration **decreases,** and vice versa.
 
• This is because transpiration is the process of **water movement** through plants from** roots to leaves**, and it occurs due to the difference in **water potential **between the soil and the atmosphere.
 
• As the atmospheric pressure **increases**, it becomes **harder** for water to **evaporate** from the leaves, and the rate of transpiration decreases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric pressure** refers to the force exerted by the **weight of the atmosphere** on the Earth's surface.

 
 
• It is measured in **units of pressure** such as **pascals or millibars.**
 
 
 
• **Transpiration** is the **loss of water **from plants through evaporation from the** leaves and stems.**
 
 
• It is an important process for plant growth and survival, as it helps to** transport nutrients and minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
 
 
• Other factors that can affect the **rate of transpiration** include** humidity, temperature, wind speed, and soil moisture.**
